population_note_text: Every debit line on a ledger under Purchase Accounts, Direct Expenses or Indirect Expenses, in the books population; credits on those ledgers that match are shown beside.

figures.definition_text: Clause 21(a) (vii) compounding an offence: the P&L debits matched as candidates, summed -- a candidate total, not a reportable amount.
Credits on the same P&L ledgers matching the (vii) compounding an offence words: shown beside, never netted.

findings.title_text: Clause 21(a) (vii) compounding an offence: candidates listed for the CA, not reported
limits_text: 1 P&L debit line(s) match the words for this item (ICAI GN ch.33 para 33.22 (Explanation 3(iii) to s.37(1): compounding an offence); the clause 21(a) candidate spec); a match is a candidate, never a conclusion, and nothing is left out for being small. The CA decides what, if anything, is reported; no clause 21(a) row is written.

Only lines on ledgers under Purchase Accounts, Direct Expenses or Indirect Expenses were searched. Keyword recall is not measured: a narration in Hindi, Hinglish or left blank is missed, and a penalty booked only in the GST cash ledger, netted in a party account, or on a credit-card statement is not in these books.
ask_client_text: Any compounding fee paid in the year? Enter it from the compounding application.
